text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised which is never answered. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; yet of what he feels we are told nothing, for the narrator never once looks within him. He neither protests nor bargains. The whole chapter turns upon Abraham's silence; he appears rather under the aspect of a silence than of a character, and shows none of the traits of the man who, on an earlier occasion, pleaded for Sodom.
